findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "read_file" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "run_sql" references sensitive artifacts (api_key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_customers, fetch_url · Private data: create_api_token, read_file, list_secrets, get_secret, rotate_keys, submit_diagnostics · Public sink: search_customers, submit_diagnostics · Destructive: kubectl, run_sql, exec_command.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_customers, fetch_url · Private data: create_api_token, read_file, list_secrets, get_secret, rotate_keys, submit_diagnostics · Public sink: search_customers, submit_diagnostics · Destructive: kubectl, run_sql, exec_command

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
